title: I Posted the Pier Fishing-Slot Roster After They Cast From My Number

parts.text: I drew slot 8 at 5:02 a.m. and a regular named Bud was already casting from 8's painted number. The roster box said: DRAW A NUMBER. FISH THE NUMBER. NO REGULARS HOLD. I was forty-nine, dawn angler, holding a chip. Bud did not move. "Regulars are the pier." I photographed the chip, the box, and his bucket on 8. Then I logged a hold. At 5:11 the harbor kiosk asked why Bud's bucket was on an undrawn 8. I let them finish the sentence they would regret in writing. Petty is a word people use when their name is on the ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The harbor kiosk can see Bud's bucket on painted 8 while my chip is the draw.

social.video_title: A regular cast from my drawn pier number — Part 1/2
social.description: Fishing pier, a chip, and a bucket on my number. I logged the hold. Would you have photographed the paint?

parts.text: Bud called it a leftover until the kiosk asked for the log. I printed the hold, the photo, and the chip. He moved. Bud drew like dawn and told the rail leftovers were always about optics. Optics is a word regulars use when a bucket exists. Slot policy now has a second line: REGULARS DRAW. I keep 8. Bud chips. The pier finally looks like a roster, not a lease. Nobody thanked me, which is how you know a policy finally works. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.

social.description: Hold log, moved bucket, and a second line. Was leftover ever my chip?
